message.content: Read redu.md and deploy Databunker on redu.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

Use when invoking models, setting up Knowledge Bases, creating agents, applying guardrails, deploying to AgentCore, troubleshooting Bedrock errors (ThrottlingException, AccessDeniedException), or choosing models (Claude, Llama, [infra], Titan). NOT for Kubernetes, EKS, or CI/CD pipelines.

Covers Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon MQ, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Data Firehose, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, and Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK). Use when implementing messaging and streaming patterns.

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). content.text: I'll start by reading redu.md.

content.content:
1	---
2	redu_schema: 2
3	repo: https://github.com/securitybunker/databunker
4	plan:
5	  tool: deploy_compose
6	  image: securitybunker/databunker:0.8.35
7	  port: 3000
8	  vm: m1.small
9	  flavor_id: "2"
10	  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
11	  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0348
12	bootstrap:
13	  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
14	  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
15	  source: databunker
16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔⛔ NEVER PASS THE demo ARGUMENT. The README quick start runs the image as securitybunker/databunker demo. That reaches run.sh:7-9, which calls the binary with -demoinit, which sets the API root token to the literal string DEMO (service.go:23,42-43). The root token is total authority over every personal record in the vault. On a public hostname that is a published credential. This recipe never uses demo mode, and if you see DEMO anywhere in a plan, stop."
18	  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: nobody signs up, and there is no first-visitor race. Databunker has no administrator account and no signup form. Authority is a single API root token presented in the X-Bunker-Token header, and it is created exactly ONCE, by the -init step, before the service ever starts. YOU SUPPLY IT: generate a UUID in your session and pass it as DATABUNKER_ROOTTOKEN (service.go:45). It must be a valid UUID or init fails with bad root token format (xtokens_db.go:31-35). This is the deploy-time case, which is the only shape that is safe by construction: the window is closed before the hostname resolves. ⛔ There is NO reset: the token is stored only as a salted hash (xtokens_db.go:43), so if the user loses it they cannot administer the vault and the records stay encrypted."
19	  - "⛔⛔ DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY IS THE SECRET A REDEPLOY DESTROYS. SET IT EXPLICITLY AND REUSE THE SAME VALUE FOREVER. It is 48 hexadecimal characters, being 24 random bytes (utils/cryptor.go:26-30), and decodeMasterkey rejects any other length or any non-hex character (service.go:150-155). Every personal record is encrypted with it and the root token hash is salted from it. Redeploy with a NEW key against the SAME managed Postgres and the init step sees the database already initialized and exits 0, the service starts cleanly, and then nothing works: the root token no longer authenticates and no record can be decrypted. There is no error and no warning at startup. This is the single most expensive mistake available here."
20	  - "⛔ SUPPLY BOTH SECRETS SO THEY NEVER LAND IN THE CONTAINER LOG. If DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY is absent at init, one is generated and PRINTED in the clear (service.go:181). If DATABUNKER_ROOTTOKEN is absent, the generated root token is PRINTED too (service.go:213). Both then sit in docker logs on the VM disk, readable by anyone with a shell. Supply both and those same two lines become Master key: **** and API Root token: [REDACTED:value] (service.go:174,211). Generate them in your session, pass them to deploy_compose as environment values, hand them to the user once, and never write either into this file."
21	  - "⛔⛔ THE DATABASE NAME IS A COMMAND LINE FLAG, NOT AN ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE, AND IT MUST BE redu's PGDATABASE. This is the one that breaks the deploy if you copy upstream. Both upstream compose files hardcode -db databunkerdb. A redu managed Postgres serves exactly ONE database, and any other name on that server is refused AT AUTHENTICATION with SQLSTATE 28000, whatever privileges the role has. So write -db ${PGDATABASE} in BOTH the init command and the start command. Get it wrong and the failure is silent in the worst way: DBExists swallows the connection error and returns false (pgsql-storage.go:59-79), the start command retries for 60 seconds, prints Database is not initialized and calls os.Exit(0) (service.go:56-66). The container stops with status ZERO, which reads as a clean shutdown rather than a failure."
22	  - "⛔ THE SILENT SQLITE FALLBACK, MADE WORSE BY THE FACT THAT redu's VARIABLE NAMES ARE NOT THE APP'S. getDBObj (storage/storage.go:107-121) chooses MySQL if MYSQL_HOST is set, Postgres if PGSQL_HOST is set, and otherwise SQLite, with no error and no warning. redu injects PGHOST, PGPORT, PGDATABASE, PGUSER and PGPASSWORD into the project .env. Databunker reads PGSQL_HOST, PGSQL_PORT, PGSQL_USER_NAME and PGSQL_USER_PASS. Passing redu's names straight through is the worst possible outcome: the app comes up perfectly healthy on a container-local SQLite file and every personal record is lost on the next redeploy. Map them yourself in the compose, PGSQL_HOST: ${PGHOST} and so on. Remember deploy_compose only APPENDS these to the project .env, it never edits your compose."
23	  - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING AFTER BOOT, WITH BOTH HALVES, BECAUSE AN ABSENCE ALONE PROVES NOTHING. On the Postgres path the start container logs POSTGRESQL Databunker db name is (pgsql-storage.go:111). On the SQLite path it logs Database file: instead (sqlite-storage.go:80). So run the POSITIVE grep first, since a non-zero count is also what tells you your command reached the log at all, and only then read the negative one. Both commands are in the body of this file under Verify the database wiring. Note the VM runs docker, not podman, and the container is named after the compose project redu unpacks into."
24	  - "⛔⛔ THE SHIPPED CONFIG LETS ANONYMOUS CALLERS WRITE PERSONAL DATA INTO YOUR VAULT, AND NO ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE CAN TURN IT OFF. The databunker.yaml baked into the image sets create_user_without_access_token to true, and users_api.go:19-24 skips the admin check entirely when it is true. On a public hostname that means anyone can POST /v1/user and create records in a database whose whole purpose is holding personal data. The field has a yaml tag and NO envconfig tag (bunker.go:38), and ReadConfFile runs AFTER ReadEnv (service.go:38-39), so the file always wins. The ONLY fix is to ship your own databunker.yaml with create_user_without_access_token: [REDACTED:value] and mount it read only at /databunker/conf/databunker.yaml. Then TEST THE BEHAVIOUR, not the flag: an anonymous POST /v1/user must be refused AND the same POST with the root token must succeed. A config dump that reports the right value is not proof."
25	  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN STILL REACH, so the user can decide whether they mind. GET /status and GET /v1/status return the body OK and ping the database. GET /v1/metrics serves Prometheus counters with no authentication at all (bunker.go, the metrics handler makes no EnforceAdmin call), which exposes request volumes but no record contents. GET /v1/sys/uiconfiguration and GET /v1/sys/cookiesettings return branding and the cookie legal basis (conf.go:14-15,48-60). / and /site/ serve the admin web UI, which is a form asking for the root token and contains no credential. Everything touching a personal record is gated: reading a user, the configuration dump at GET /v1/sys/configuration and the WHOLE DATABASE BACKUP at GET /v1/sys/backup all call EnforceAdmin or EnforceAuth and answer 403 Access denied without a valid token (bunker.go:146-152, conf.go:36-45, audit_api.go:100-127)."
26	  - "DELETE THE BUNDLED POSTGRES FROM THE UPSTREAM COMPOSE, BUT KEEP BOTH DATABUNKER SERVICES. docker-compose-pgsql.yml ships its own postgres service with a self-signed certificate produced by generate-pgsql-env-files.sh and a setup-postgresql.sh init hook. On redu the managed Postgres replaces all of that: delete the postgresql service, its volume, the .env files it reads and the whole certificate dance. Do NOT collapse the two Databunker services into one: databunker-init runs once and creates the ten tables, databunker runs forever. Re-running init is idempotent, printing Database is alredy initialized. (upstream's spelling) and exiting 0 (service.go:47-55), so it is safe on every redeploy. Gate the long-running service on it with depends_on condition service_completed_successfully."
27	  - "OVERRIDE THE IMAGE ENTRYPOINT. run.sh is the image ENTRYPOINT and it is SQLite-only: it decides whether to initialise by testing for the file /databunker/data/databunker.db (run.sh:5). With PGSQL_HOST set that file never appears, so run.sh tries to init a POSTGRES database literally named /databunker/data/databunker.db, fails, sleeps 60 seconds and exits. Both upstream compose files override entrypoint to /bin/sh and pass the real command, and so must yours. A useful side effect: with the entrypoint overridden, run.sh's echo of the generated keys never happens either."
28	  - "PORT 3000, PLAIN HTTP, AND DO NOT SET SSL_CERTIFICATE. databunker.yaml sets server host 0.0.0.0 and port 3000, and the Dockerfile exposes 3000. service.go:131-143 opens an HTTPS listener only when the file named by ssl.ssl_certificate exists; the image creates /databunker/certs empty and puts no certificate in it, so it listens on plain HTTP, which is exactly what redu needs. redu terminates TLS at its own proxy and forwards HTTP to the VM, so setting SSL_CERTIFICATE or mounting a certificate breaks the deploy rather than hardening it. Pass port 3000 to deploy_compose. Health probe: GET /v1/status, which must be 200 with a body of OK, and which also pings the database, so it is a real check rather than a static string."
29	  - "⛔ PIN 0.8.35, NOT THE VERSION THE REPO CLAIMS. version.txt on master says 0.8.36, and on Docker Hub, measured 2026-08-17, THE TAG 0.8.36 DOES NOT EXIST. The repository has eight tags: latest, 0.8.35, 0.8.35-amd64, 0.8.36-arm64, 0.8.35-arm64, 0.8.34, 0.8.34-amd64 and 0.8.34-arm64. Both 0.8.36 and 0.8.36-amd64 answer 404, and a negative control on a tag that certainly does not exist answered 404 the same way, so the 404 is real rather than a broken query. redu VMs are amd64, so 0.8.36-arm64 would pull an image that cannot run. latest and 0.8.35 currently resolve to the same digest, which is another reason not to write latest: it is a moving alias for whatever ships next. Pin securitybunker/databunker:0.8.35."
30	  - "THERE IS NOTHING TO PERSIST ON A VOLUME EXCEPT YOUR OWN CONFIG FILE. With PGSQL_HOST set, every record lives in the managed Postgres and /databunker/data is never touched. Do not mount a volume there and then believe it is a backup, because it is empty. The only thing to bind mount is the databunker.yaml you wrote, read only. What genuinely must survive, and lives outside the platform entirely, is the master key and the root token."
31	  - "NO migrate_command, AND db_superuser IS NOT NEEDED EITHER. The init service creates its ten tables through InitDB (storage/pgsql-storage.go:147-160). Databunker never issues CREATE DATABASE against your server, so the default managed role is sufficient and you should not ask for superuser you do not need."
32	  - "SSLMODE IS NOT CONFIGURABLE FROM DATABUNKER, SO KNOW WHERE THE KNOB IS. getConnectionString (pgsql-storage.go:53-54) sets only user, password, host, port and dbname; it never sets sslmode, so the driver's own default applies. redu's managed Postgres has been verified TLS capable on another entry in this library, so the default is expected to connect. If you ever see SSL is not enabled on the server, the fix is the libpq environment variable in the container, not a Databunker setting, because Databunker has no setting for it."
33	  - "SIZING AND PRICE ARE REASONING, NOT MEASUREMENT, AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO FIGURE. The image is a single statically linked Go binary on a scratch base with busybox beside it, and the repository documents no memory or CPU requirement anywhere. On that basis m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) is a sensible floor, which puts the whole deploy at about GBP 0.035 an hour with the managed Postgres, inside the no-card free trial. NOT YET DEPLOYED BY REDU: measure the real figure on your run and write it back here instead of repeating this paragraph."

154	  echo "Do not leave this instance up until you know which."

160	#    the endpoint exists and the request shape is right. Without this, a refusal

  - "⛔⛔ NEVER PASS THE demo ARGUMENT. The README quick start runs the image as securitybunker/databunker demo. The root token is total authority over every personal record in the vault. On a public hostname that is a published credential. This recipe never uses demo mode, and if you see DEMO anywhere in a plan, stop."
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: nobody signs up, and there is no first-visitor race. Databunker has no administrator account and no signup form. Authority is a single API root token presented in the X-Bunker-Token header, and it is created exactly ONCE, by the -init step, before the service ever starts. YOU SUPPLY IT: generate a UUID in your session and pass it as DATABUNKER_ROOTTOKEN (service.go:45). It must be a valid UUID or init fails with bad root token format (xtokens_db.go:31-35). This is the deploy-time case, which is the only shape that is safe by construction: the window is closed before the hostname resolves. ⛔ There is NO reset: the token is stored only as a salted hash (xtokens_db.go:43), so if the user loses it they cannot administer the vault and the records stay encrypted."
  - "⛔⛔ DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY IS THE SECRET A REDEPLOY DESTROYS. SET IT EXPLICITLY AND REUSE THE SAME VALUE FOREVER. It is 48 hexadecimal characters, being 24 random bytes (utils/cryptor.go:26-30), and decodeMasterkey rejects any other length or any non-hex character (service.go:150-155). Every personal record is encrypted with it and the root token hash is salted from it. Redeploy with a NEW key against the SAME managed Postgres and the init step sees the database already initialized and exits 0, the service starts cleanly, and then nothing works: the root token no longer authenticates and no record can be decrypted. There is no error and no warning at startup. This is the single most expensive mistake available here."
  - "⛔ SUPPLY BOTH SECRETS SO THEY NEVER LAND IN THE CONTAINER LOG. If DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY is absent at init, one is generated and PRINTED in the clear (service.go:181). If DATABUNKER_ROOTTOKEN is absent, the generated root token is PRINTED too (service.go:213). Both then sit in docker logs on the VM disk, readable by anyone with a shell. Supply both and those same two lines become Master key: **** and API Root token: [REDACTED:value] (service.go:174,211).   - "⛔⛔ THE DATABASE NAME IS A COMMAND LINE FLAG, NOT AN ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE, AND IT MUST BE redu's PGDATABASE. This is the one that breaks the deploy if you copy upstream. Both upstream compose files hardcode -db databunkerdb. A redu managed Postgres serves exactly ONE database, and any other name on that server is refused AT AUTHENTICATION with SQLSTATE 28000, whatever privileges the role has. So write -db ${PGDATABASE} in BOTH the init command and the start command. Get it wrong and the failure is silent in the worst way: DBExists swallows the connection error and returns false (pgsql-storage.go:59-79), the start command retries for 60 seconds, prints Database is not initialized and calls os.Exit(0) (service.go:56-66).   - "⛔ THE SILENT SQLITE FALLBACK, MADE WORSE BY THE FACT THAT redu's VARIABLE NAMES ARE NOT THE APP'S. getDBObj (storage/storage.go:107-121) chooses MySQL if MYSQL_HOST is set, Postgres if PGSQL_HOST is set, and otherwise SQLite, with no error and no warning. redu injects PGHOST, PGPORT, PGDATABASE, PGUSER and PGPASSWORD into the project .env.   - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING AFTER BOOT, WITH BOTH HALVES, BECAUSE AN ABSENCE ALONE PROVES NOTHING. Both commands are in the body of this file under Verify the database wiring. Note the VM runs docker, not podman, and the container is named after the compose project redu unpacks into."
  - "⛔⛔ THE SHIPPED CONFIG LETS ANONYMOUS CALLERS WRITE PERSONAL DATA INTO YOUR VAULT, AND NO ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE CAN TURN IT OFF. On a public hostname that means anyone can POST /v1/user and create records in a database whose whole purpose is holding personal data.   - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN STILL REACH, so the user can decide whether they mind. GET /status and GET /v1/status return the body OK and ping the database. GET /v1/metrics serves Prometheus counters with no authentication at all (bunker.go, the metrics handler makes no EnforceAdmin call), which exposes request volumes but no record contents. GET /v1/sys/uiconfiguration and GET /v1/sys/cookiesettings return branding and the cookie legal basis (conf.go:14-15,48-60). / and /site/ serve the admin web UI, which is a form asking for the root token and contains no credential.   - "DELETE THE BUNDLED POSTGRES FROM THE UPSTREAM COMPOSE, BUT KEEP BOTH DATABUNKER SERVICES. docker-compose-pgsql.yml ships its own postgres service with a self-signed certificate produced by generate-pgsql-env-files.sh and a setup-postgresql.sh init hook. On redu the managed Postgres replaces all of that: delete the postgresql service, its volume, the .env files it reads and the whole certificate dance. Do NOT collapse the two Databunker services into one: databunker-init runs once and creates the ten tables, databunker runs forever. Re-running init is idempotent, printing Database is alredy initialized. (upstream's spelling) and exiting 0 (service.go:47-55), so it is safe on every redeploy. Gate the long-running service on it with depends_on condition service_completed_successfully."
  - "OVERRIDE THE IMAGE ENTRYPOINT. run.sh is the image ENTRYPOINT and it is SQLite-only: it decides whether to initialise by testing for the file /databunker/data/databunker.db (run.sh:5). With PGSQL_HOST set that file never appears, so run.sh tries to init a POSTGRES database literally named /databunker/data/databunker.db, fails, sleeps 60 seconds and exits. fi
if [ "$lite" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: this instance is on SQLite. Every record dies at the next redeploy."
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: Databunker is on the managed Postgres."
```

## Verify that anonymous callers cannot write to the vault

This is the security-critical check, so it proves the negative with a positive control beside it.
redu's hostname answers 502 for roughly the first two and a half minutes while the container
starts, and an error page fails every assertion of the form "did it NOT do X", so the script
refuses to conclude anything until it has proved it is talking to Databunker.

```bash
set -u
: "${HOST:?set HOST to the deployed hostname}"
: "${ROOTTOKEN:[REDACTED:value] ROOTTOKEN to the root token you generated at init}"
OUT=$(mktemp)

# 1. Prove we are talking to Databunker, not to the proxy's error page.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$OUT" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/v1/status")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "502 from the proxy: still starting, re-run in a minute"
  exit 2
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ] || [ "$(cat "$OUT")" != "OK" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /v1/status answered $code, body was not OK"
  exit 2
fi
echo "ok: /v1/status is 200 OK, so the app is up and its database ping succeeded"

# 2. POSITIVE: the root token authenticates on the admin surface.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$OUT" -w '%{http_code}' -H "X-Bunker-Token: [REDACTED:value]" \
  "https://$HOST/v1/sys/configuration")
if [ "$code" != "200" ] || ! grep -q 'configuration' "$OUT"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the config dump answered $code. Wrong token, or the route moved."
  echo "Do not leave this instance up until you know which."
  exit 2
fi
echo "ok: the root token authenticates"

# 3. POSITIVE CONTROL: an AUTHENTICATED create must succeed, which is what proves
#    the endpoint exists and the request shape is right. Without this, a refusal
#    in step 4 could just mean a malformed body or a moved route.
code=$(printf '%s' '{"login":"redu-probe","first":"redu","last":"probe"}' \
  | curl -sS -o "$OUT" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
      -H "X-Bunker-Token: [REDACTED:value]" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/v1/user")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: an authenticated create answered $code, so step 4 would prove nothing"
  exit 2
fi
REC=$(sed -n 's/.*"token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' "$OUT")
echo "ok: an authenticated create works, record $REC"

# 4. NEGATIVE: the same create with NO token must be refused.
code=$(printf '%s' '{"login":"redu-anon-probe","first":"anon","last":"probe"}' \
  | curl -sS -o "$OUT" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/v1/user")
if [ "$code" = "200" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: anonymous callers can write personal data into this vault."
  echo "      create_user_without_access_token is still true. Fix the config file and redeploy."
  exit 1
fi
echo "ok: an anonymous create is refused with $code"

# 5. Remove the probe record.
curl -sS -o /dev/null -X DELETE -H "X-Bunker-Token: [REDACTED:value]" \
  "https://$HOST/v1/user/token/$REC"
rm -f "$OUT"
echo "all checks passed"
```

Do NOT read or summarise them - redu parses them SERVER-SIDE and returns a short digest, a pin_dname that keeps a redeploy on the SAME public URL, and preflight fixes for known failure patterns in YOUR repo. Highest-value step in the flow; it costs one cat each. platform_facts: THE deploy VM RUNS DOCKER, NOT PODMAN. The compose project is named app-src, so containers are app-src-<service>-1 and volumes are app-src_<name>. Use `sudo docker ...` on the VM; podman is not installed. Several deploys rediscovered this independently.

SOURCE IS EITHER GIT OR UPLOAD, NEVER BOTH. For code that is not pushed, or is private, or needs fixing first: write the files locally, call prepare_upload, run the tar+curl block it returns, then pass the source_token and NO repo. ⚠️ prepare_upload EXCLUDES .env from the tarball by design, so secrets have to reach the VM another way (pass them to the deploy call, not in the tree).

A MANAGED DATABASE IS A SECOND VM WITH ITS OWN HOURLY RATE, and delete_deployment deliberately LEAVES IT BEHIND so your data survives the app. That means a teardown that stops at delete_deployment keeps billing a database nobody can reach. Call delete_database too, and say so to the user before either.

A MANAGED POSTGRES SERVES EXACTLY ONE DATABASE. pg_hba is evaluated before role privileges, so being superuser does not help. An app that wants a second database needs a second managed server. This has broken deploys that otherwise looked healthy.

get_deployment RETURNS THE MERGED redu.md ONLY WHEN IT FITS ITS RESPONSE BUDGET. Over budget - which is normal for a mature recipe or any large app - it withholds redu_md_markdown and returns redu_md_last_deploy_block plus redu_md_deploy_log_line instead. That is NOT an error and must not be retried: apply those two edits to the file on disk and change nothing else.

⛔ THE MERGE NEVER WRITES A NEW QUIRK. Whatever redu returns, it refreshes last_deploy and appends one deploy-log line and nothing else. Every gotcha YOUR run discovered has to be typed into the quirks list by hand before you commit, or it is lost - and that list is the only part of the file that makes the next deploy cheaper.
⛔ NEVER WRITE A CREDENTIAL INTO redu.md. It is committed and read by the next person and the next agent. Names of variables, yes; their values, never. Hand secrets to the user in the session instead.

plan_deploy OVER-SIZES A PULLED COMPOSE STACK. Measured 8 times out of 8: declaring needs_compose makes it quote m1.large, roughly double the real requirement, because it cannot see that the images are pulled rather than built. Show the user the plan, but size from the app's real memory figure when you have one.

THE MANAGED DATABASE PASSWORD IS ON THE VM, NOT IN THE API. list_databases returns private_ip, port, db_name and db_user and DELIBERATELY NOT the password, so an agent that looks for it there finds nothing and starts guessing. The deploy writes the whole connection set into the compose project's .env on the app VM: SSH in (get_ssh_command) and read the NAMES first, `sudo grep -oE '^[A-Z_]+=' /opt/app-src/.env`, then the one value you need. ⚠️ That file is chmod 600 root:root so it needs sudo, and the database is on the PRIVATE network - reachable from the app VM, never from a laptop.

# Server configurations
generic:
  # allow to create user object without login
  create_user_without_access_token: [REDACTED:value]
  # use separate app tables, default false
  # use_separate_app_tables: true
  # specify if API call to list users is available (default false)
  # list_users: true
  # disable audit, default false

selfservice:
  # specifies if user can remove himself withour Admin/DPO approval (default false)
  #forget_me: false
  # specifies if user can change his data without Admin/DPO approval (default false)
  #user_record_change: true
  # specifies a list of app-data objects user can change without approval
  app_record_change: ["*"]
notification:
  # url that receives notifications:
  # - bad login
  # - forget me
  # - user profile change
  # - consent change
  # user details are send as json data.

policy:
  # max time to store records, untill they are deleted
  max_user_retention_period: "3m"
  max_audit_retention_period: "6m"
  max_session_retention_period: "1h"
  max_shareable_record_retention_period: "1m"

=== RUN.SH ===
#!/bin/sh

#/bin/busybox find /databunker

if [ ! -f /databunker/data/databunker.db ]; then
  OPTION="-init"
  if [ "$1" == "demo" ]; then
    OPTION="-demoinit"
  fi
  echo "-------------------------------------------------"
  echo "run.sh: init database, encryption, and access keys"
  #/bin/busybox mkdir -p /tmp
  RESULT=`/databunker/bin/databunker $OPTION -db /databunker/data/databunker.db -conf /databunker/conf/databunker.yaml > /tmp/init.txt 2>&1`
  if [ ! -f /databunker/data/databunker.db ]; then
    echo "Failed to init databunker database. Probably permission issue for /databunker/data directory."
    /bin/busybox sleep 60
    exit
  fi
  /bin/busybox cat /tmp/init.txt
  DATABUNKER_ROOTTOKEN=«REDACTED:assigned:3f21cdcf» awk '/API Root token:/ {print $6}' /tmp/init.txt`
  DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY2=`/bin/busybox awk '/Master key:/ {print $5}' /tmp/init.txt`
  echo "DATABUNKER_ROOTTOKEN $DATABUNKER_ROOTTOKEN"
  echo "DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY $DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY2"
  /bin/busybox rm -rf /tmp/init.txt
  if [ -z "$DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY" ]; then
    echo "export DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY=$DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY2"
    export DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY=$DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY2
  fi
fi
if [ -z "$DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY" ]; then
  echo "DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY environment value is empty"
  /bin/busybox sleep 60
  exit
fi
echo "-------------------------------------------------"
echo "run.sh: shart databunker service"
/databunker/bin/databunker -start -db /databunker/data/databunker.db -conf /databunker/conf/databunker.yaml
=== DOCKERFILE ===
##############################
# STEP 1 build executable file
##############################
FROM golang:alpine AS builder
RUN apk update && apk add --no-cache git gcc libc-dev openssl && go install github.com/gobuffalo/packr/packr@latest
WORKDIR /go/src/securitybunker/databunker/src/
COPY src/go.mod ./go.mod
#RUN cat ./deps | grep -v storage | grep -v utils | grep -v audit > ./go.mod && go mod download
RUN go mod download
COPY . /go/src/securitybunker/databunker/
WORKDIR /go/src/securitybunker/databunker/
#RUN echo "tidy " && go get -u && go mod tidy && cat ./go.mod
RUN ./build.sh
#################################
# STEP 2 create a small container
#################################
FROM scratch
COPY --from=builder /bin/sh /bin/busybox /usr/bin/openssl /bin/
COPY --from=builder /lib/ld* /lib/libssl.* /lib/libcrypto.* /lib/
COPY --from=builder /etc/group /etc/
COPY --from=builder /etc/ssl /etc/ssl

COPY databunker.yaml /databunker/conf/
RUN /bin/busybox mkdir -p /databunker/data && \
    /bin/busybox mkdir -p /databunker/certs && \
    /bin/busybox ln -s /bin/busybox /bin/addgroup && \
    /bin/busybox ln -s /bin/busybox /bin/adduser && \
    /bin/busybox ln -s /bin/busybox /bin/chown && \
    /bin/busybox touch /etc/passwd && \
    /bin/busybox mkdir -p /tmp && \
    /bin/busybox chmod 0777 /tmp && \
    addgroup -S appgroup && adduser --no-create-home -S appuser -G appgroup && \
    chown appuser:appgroup /databunker/data
VOLUME ["/databunker/data"]
USER appuser
COPY --from=builder /go/src/securitybunker/databunker/databunker /go/src/securitybunker/databunker/run.sh /go/src/securitybunker/databunker/health-check.sh /databunker/bin/
EXPOSE 3000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=5s --timeout=3s --start-period=33s --retries=3 CMD /databunker/bin/health-check.sh
ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/sh", "/databunker/bin/run.sh"]
#CMD ["/bin/sh", "-x", "-c", "/go/bin/databunker -init"]

"# Databunker on redu — managed Postgres, no bundled database.
#
# Two services on purpose: databunker-init runs once and creates the tables,

# Databunker configuration for the redu deploy.
# This is upstream's databunker.yaml with ONE deliberate change:
# create_user_without_access_token is false. The image ships it as true, which
# lets any anonymous caller POST /v1/user into the vault, and no environment
# variable can override it (the field has no envconfig tag, and the conf file is
# read after the environment). Mounting this file read-only is the only fix.
generic:
  # allow to create user object without login
  create_user_without_access_token: [REDACTED:value]
  # use separate app tables, default false
  # use_separate_app_tables: true
  # specify if API call to list users is available (default false)
  # list_users: true
  # disable audit, default false
  # disable_audit: true
selfservice:
  # specifies if user can remove himself withour Admin/DPO approval (default false)
  #forget_me: false
  # specifies if user can change his data without Admin/DPO approval (default false)
  #user_record_change: true
  # specifies a list of app-data objects user can change without approval
  app_record_change: ["*"]
notification:
  # url that receives notifications:
  # - bad login
  # - forget me
  # - user profile change
  # - consent change
  # user details are send as json data.
  #notification_url: "https://httpbin.org/post"
policy:
  # max time to store records, untill they are deleted
  # NOTE: the suffix "m" is MONTHS here, not minutes (utils.ParseExpiration0).
  # This is the ceiling applied when an admin initiates a record expiration;
  # records do not expire on their own.
  max_user_retention_period: "3m"
  max_audit_retention_period: "6m"
  max_session_retention_period: "1h"
  max_shareable_record_retention_period: "1m"
ssl:
  # No certificate is shipped in the image and none is mounted, so Databunker
  # listens on plain HTTP on 3000. redu terminates TLS at its own proxy.
  # Do NOT point these at a real file: it breaks the deploy rather than
  # hardening it.
  ssl_certificate: "/databunker/certs/server.cer"
  ssl_certificate_key: "/databunker/certs/server.key"
sms:
  # default country when sending out SMS

server:
  host: "0.0.0.0"
  port: 3000

  # Set these if you want Databunker to send login/notification email.

  port: 587
  user: "user@your-company.com"
  pass: ""
  sender: "bot@databunker.your-company.com"

  logo_link: "/site/img/logo-example.png"
  company_title: "Your company here"
  company_link: "https://databunker.org/"
  term_of_service_title: "Your Terms of service link"
  term_of_service_link: "https://databunker.org/"
  privacy_policy_title: "Your Privacy Policy link"
  privacy_policy_link: "https://databunker.org/"

Nothing here is built: both services pull the same pinned image, and the binary is a single static Go binary on a `scratch` base. `redu.md` records **m1.small** as the intended size, so `flavor_id: "2"` is passed explicitly. `db_flavor_id: "2"` is passed explicitly too — omitting it would default the database VM to the app flavor and double the bill. ## What gets deployed ```mermaid flowchart LR user([User]) -->|https| ap["Access point

m1.small — 1 vCPU / 2 GB

## Databunker on redu — the plan

**Two m1.small VMs:** the app VM (init container + long-running container, port 3000) and a managed Postgres on the private network holding every encrypted record.

Inside the no-card free trial. Billed hourly, deletable anytime.

**A sizing note:** `plan_deploy` wanted m1.large (£48/mo) because it sees a multi-service compose and assumes a build. Nothing is built here — both services pull the same pinned image of a static Go binary. I'm passing `flavor_id: "2"` and `db_flavor_id: "2"` explicitly to hold m1.small, exactly as `redu.md` instructs. That also brings it inside your vCPU quota; the m1.large plan did not fit.

**Files written locally** (`docker-compose.yml`, `databunker.yaml`, `redu-deploy-plan.md`) — upload mode, no git, since upstream's Dockerfile would compile Go on the VM. I verified every claim in `redu.md` against upstream source rather than trusting it: the `PGSQL_*` vs `PG*` mapping, `-db ${PGDATABASE}` as a flag in both commands, the SQLite-only entrypoint that must be overridden, and `create_user_without_access_token` having a yaml tag but no envconfig tag — so mounting my own config is genuinely the only fix.

**No `migrate_command`** — the init service creates the schema itself.

**Two secrets, generated in this session, that you must keep:**
- `DATABUNKER_ROOTTOKEN` — total authority over the vault. No reset; stored only as a salted hash.
- `DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY` — 48 hex chars. **Reuse this exact value on every future redeploy.** A new key against the same database gives you a service that starts perfectly and can decrypt nothing.

I'll pass both to `deploy_compose` as environment values so they never land in the container log, and hand them to you once here after deploy. They go into no file.

Shall I go ahead and deploy?
Approved — deploying. First, package the local directory.

  echo "      create_user_without_access_token is still true. Fix the config file and redeploy."

After the deploy reaches `ready`, > replace this file with `get_deployment()`'s `report_markdown`, which carries the REAL > deployed URL, VM id, port and managed-DB name. **App:** Databunker `securitybunker/databunker:0.8.35` — two-container compose stack, port 3000 **Deploy tool:** `deploy_compose`, upload mode (no git — upstream's Dockerfile compiles Go from source) **Feasibility:** fits quota (2 instances, 2 vCPU, 4 GB) ## Sizing override `plan_deploy` sized the app VM at **m1.large** because it sees a multi-service compose and assumes a build. Nothing here is built: both services pull the same pinned image, and the binary is a single static Go binary on a `scratch` base. `redu.md` records **m1.small** as the intended size, so `flavor_id: "2"` is passed explicitly. `db_flavor_id: "2"` is passed explicitly too — omitting it would default the database VM to the app flavor and double the bill. ## What gets deployed ```mermaid flowchart LR user([User]) -->|https| ap["Access point
<name>.redu.cloud"] ap --> app subgraph net["your private network"] app["App VM x1
m1.small — 1 vCPU / 2 GB
databunker-init (once) + databunker"] pg[("Managed postgres
m1.small — 1 vCPU / 2 GB")] end app -->|"5432 (private)"| pg ``` - **databunker-init** runs once, creates the ten tables, exits 0. Idempotent on every redeploy. - **databunker** runs forever, gated on init with `condition: service_completed_successfully`. - **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM holds every encrypted record. No bundled postgres, no volume — with `PGSQL_HOST` set, `/databunker/data` is never touched. - **`databunker.yaml`** mounted read-only with `create_user_without_access_token: «REDACTED:assigned:b4673e57» ## Cost — billed hourly, delete anytime | Resource | Rate | Monthly (est. 730h) | |---|---|---| | App VM — m1.small | GBP 0.0174/hr | GBP 12.70/mo | | Managed Postgres — m1.small | GBP 0.0174/hr | GBP 12.70/mo | | **Total** | **GBP 0.0348/hr** | **GBP 25.40/mo** | _Egress is usage-based and not included. Inside the no-card free trial._ ## Preflight, answered | Check | Answer | |---|---| | Listens on 0.0.0.0 | Yes — `databunker.yaml` sets `server.host: 0.0.0.0`, port 3000. | | Starts on every boot | Yes — `restart: unless-stopped` on the long-running service. | | Schema on first boot | Yes — the `databunker-init` service creates the tables via `InitDB`. **No `migrate_command` needed.** | | Slow start | Expected; do not retry on `building` before the probe window closes. | | Flavor differs from record | Deliberate — holding m1.small per `redu.md`. See above. | ## The three things that actually break this deploy, and how they are handled 1. **Database name** — `-db ${PGDATABASE}` in *both* the init and start commands. A redu managed Postgres serves exactly one database; any other name is refused at authentication and the container exits with status **zero**. 2. **Variable names** — Databunker reads `PGSQL_*`, redu injects `PG*`. The compose maps them. Unmapped, the app silently runs on container-local SQLite and loses everything on redeploy. 3. **Shipped config** — the image's `databunker.yaml` allows anonymous record creation and no environment variable can turn it off. Our own file is mounted read-only at `/databunker/conf/databunker.yaml`. ## Two secrets, generated in-session `DATABUNKER_ROOTTOKEN` (UUID) and `DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY` (48 hex chars) are generated locally and passed to `deploy_compose` as environment values, so the container never prints them to its log. They are handed to the user in the session and written to **no file**. The master key must be reused verbatim on every future redeploy against this same database. _Generated by redu plan_deploy, adjusted for the recorded m1.small sizing. Confirm before provisioning._

  - "✅ THE DEPLOY IS IDEMPOTENT AT THE INIT STEP AND THE EVIDENCE IS IN TWO LOGS, NOT ONE. The masked lines are the proof that supplying both secrets worked, so READ THE INIT CONTAINER'S LOG, not just the service's. The compose project is app-src, so the containers are app-src-databunker-init-1 and app-src-databunker-1."
  - "THE IMAGE'S OWN HEALTHCHECK SURVIVES THE ENTRYPOINT OVERRIDE AND IS FINE. health-check.sh looks for a certificate in three places, finds none, and falls back to wget on http://localhost:3000/status, so docker reports the long-running container as (healthy) on the plain-HTTP path.   - "DELETE /v1/user/token/<token> LEAVES A TOMBSTONE, SO THE CLEANUP STEP OF THE PROBE SCRIPT DOES NOT MAKE THE RECORD VANISH. The personal data is gone, which is what forget-me means here, but the token row remains and a 404 is the wrong thing to assert. Deployed and verified.

## Databunker is live

**https://databunker-t8agpc9v.redu.cloud** — admin UI at `/`, API at `/v1/*`.

**£0.0348/hr (~£25.40/mo)** — app VM £0.0174 + managed Postgres £0.0174. The measured figure matches what `redu.md` reasoned to before deployment. Deploy #451, ~5 minutes end to end.

## Your two secrets — save these now

```
DATABUNKER_ROOTTOKEN = «REDACTED:assigned:5ee4b8b0»
DATABUNKER_MASTERKEY = «REDACTED:longhex:00f7953e»
```

The root token is total authority over the vault — pass it as `X-Bunker-Token`. There is no reset; it's stored only as a salted hash. The master key must be reused **verbatim** on any future redeploy against this same database; a new one gives you a service that starts perfectly and decrypts nothing. Neither value is in any file, and both show as `****` in the container log — I verified that.

## Verifications, both passed

**Database wiring** — `POSTGRESQL Databunker db name is: app`, all ten tables created, **zero** SQLite lines. Init container exited 0; service container is `Up (healthy)`.

**Anonymous writes refused** — with positive controls beside the negative, so the refusal means something: `/v1/status` 200 `OK` → root token authenticates → authenticated `POST /v1/user` succeeds → the same POST with no token gets **403 Access denied**.

## Two things worth knowing

**The database is named `app`, not `databunker`.** redu's report calls it `databunker` — that's the resource name; the actual `PGDATABASE` is `app`. Anyone reading the report and hardcoding `-db databunker` would hit exactly the silent exit-zero failure the recipe warns about. Using `${PGDATABASE}` made this a non-event.

**The probe record left a tombstone.** After the cleanup DELETE, `GET /v1/user/token/30933400-…` still returns 200 with `"data":{}`. The personal data is gone — that's forget-me semantics — but the token row remains. The recipe's script doesn't check this, so I'm flagging it rather than letting you find it later.

## Files

`docker-compose.yml` and `databunker.yaml` written locally (upload mode — upstream's Dockerfile would compile Go on the VM). `redu-deploy-plan.md` now holds the real deployed values.

I **did not** overwrite `redu.md` with redu's merged output: I'd passed a condensed version of the quirks to the merge, so writing it back would have stripped the original's source line numbers and detail. I hand-edited instead — `last_deploy` added, deploy log appended, the sizing paragraph updated from reasoning to measurement, and 7 new quirks this run actually taught (the `app` database name, `plan_deploy`'s infeasible-verdict artifact, the tombstone, the control plane 502ing mid-deploy while the deploy was fine, and the TLS-unrecognized-name phase that precedes the 502). Frontmatter validated: 28 quirks, parses clean, no secrets.

One caveat on teardown: `delete_deployment` leaves the managed Postgres running and billing — and it holds the personal data. `delete_database` (id 143) is the one that removes the records.

content.text:
Yes — fully usable. SMTP touches exactly two functions in the whole codebase (`email.go`), and neither is on the path your application uses.

**What needs no email at all:** everything driven by the root token. Creating, reading, updating and deleting user records, tokenization, consents and agreements, the audit log, `/v1/sys/backup`. That's the entire API surface an app integrates against — and it's already proven working on your instance, since the authenticated `POST /v1/user` in the verification succeeded with SMTP pointed at a placeholder host.

**What SMTP actually gates:** one thing — the *data subject's own* self-service login by email, `GET /v1/prelogin/email/:identity/...`. That's the flow where an end user proves who they are with a one-time code so they can view or erase their own record without you mediating. The code is generated and stored; it just never gets delivered.

**One trap worth knowing.** That send is fired as a goroutine (`go sendCodeByEmail(...)`, `users_api.go:326`) and the handler returns `200 {"status":"ok","result":"done"}` regardless. So a broken SMTP config looks identical to a working one from the API. The only evidence is `Error sending email:` in `docker logs app-src-databunker-1`. Don't test that flow by status code.

The second call site, `adminEmailAlert`, no-ops because `admin_email` is unset — and it's guarded by `if err != nil` on record creation, so it only fires when a request *fails to save*, which looks like an upstream bug rather than the notification you'd expect.

## Covering the self-service gap without SMTP

**Admin-mediated** — no third party at all. Your app holds the root token and performs the read/change/delete on the user's behalf. GDPR requests land in `/v1/requests` for approval through the admin UI. For most self-hosted deployments this is the whole answer.

**SMS instead of email** — `sendCodeByPhone` doesn't use SMTP; it POSTs to an HTTP gateway URL from the `sms:` config block, with `_PHONE_`/`_MSG_`/`_TOKEN_` placeholders, so any provider works. `/v1/prelogin/phone/...` is then fully functional.

**The notification webhook** — `notification_url` in the config posts JSON on new profile, profile change, forget-me and consent change. It gives you the notifications email would have carried, and it no-ops cleanly when unset (`notify.go:25-27`).

## Adding SMTP later is cheap and safe

`databunker.yaml` is a read-only bind mount, not baked into the image. So it's edit the file on the VM and restart one container:

```
sudo vi /opt/app-src/databunker.yaml       # fill in the smtp: block
cd /opt/app-src && sudo docker compose restart databunker
```

No re-init, no redeploy, no tarball upload — and critically, nothing touches the master key or the root token. This is the one change class here that carries none of the redeploy risk.

Right now the config carries upstream's placeholder (`email-smtp-server.com`, empty password). Want me to strip that block so a stray prelogin attempt fails quietly instead of logging connection errors against a fake host — or wire up a `notification_url` if you have an endpoint for it?

# read after the environment). Mounting this file read-only is the only fix.
generic:
  # allow to create user object without login
  create_user_without_access_token: [REDACTED:value]
  # use separate app tables, default false
  # use_separate_app_tables: true
  # specify if API call to list users is available (default false)
  # list_users: true
  # disable audit, default false
  # disable_audit: true
selfservice:
  # specifies if user can remove himself withour Admin/DPO approval (default false)
  #forget_me: false
  # specifies if user can change his data without Admin/DPO approval (default false)
  #user_record_change: true
  # specifies a list of app-data objects user can change without approval
  app_record_change: ["*"]
notification:
  # url that receives notifications:
  # - bad login
  # - forget me
  # - user profile change
  # - consent change
  # user details are send as json data.
  #notification_url: "https://httpbin.org/post"
policy:
  # max time to store records, untill they are deleted
  # NOTE: the suffix "m" is MONTHS here, not minutes (utils.ParseExpiration0).
  # This is the ceiling applied when an admin initiates a record expiration;
  # records do not expire on their own.
  max_user_retention_period: "3m"
  max_audit_retention_period: "6m"
  max_session_retention_period: "1h"
  max_shareable_record_retention_period: "1m"
ssl:
  # No certificate is shipped in the image and none is mounted, so Databunker
  # listens on plain HTTP on 3000. redu terminates TLS at its own proxy.
  # Do NOT point these at a real file: it breaks the deploy rather than
  # hardening it.
  ssl_certificate: "/databunker/certs/server.cer"
  ssl_certificate_key: "/databunker/certs/server.key"
sms:
  # default country when sending out SMS
  default_country: "GB"
server:
  host: "0.0.0.0"
  port: 3000
# NO SMTP, DELIBERATELY AND PERMANENTLY.
#
# Upstream ships an smtp: block pointing at the placeholder host
# email-smtp-server.com with an empty password. That placeholder is worse than
# nothing: it makes every send attempt dial a real, foreign hostname before
# failing. This deployment does not send email and is not going to, so the block
# is removed rather than left half-filled.

# route still answers 200 {"status":"ok","result":"done"} either way, because
# the send is a goroutine (users_api.go:326) whose error only reaches the log —
# so do not read that 200 as "mail was sent".
#
# What this does NOT cost: the entire root-token API. Creating, reading,
# updating and deleting records, tokenization, consents, agreements, audit and
# backup never touch SMTP.
#
# The alternatives, if self-service login is ever wanted, are the sms: gateway
# below (plain HTTP to any provider, not SMTP) or a notification_url webhook.
#
# ⛔ Do not reintroduce an smtp: block here on a later edit or redeploy.
ui:
  logo_link: "/site/img/logo-example.png"
  company_title: "Your company here"
  company_link: "https://databunker.org/"
  term_of_service_title: "Your Terms of service link"
  term_of_service_link: "https://databunker.org/"
  privacy_policy_title: "Your Privacy Policy link"
  privacy_policy_link: "https://databunker.org/"
  custom_css_link: ""

content.text:
Done — both blocks are gone, live and locally.

## What changed

`databunker.yaml` no longer has an `smtp:` or an `sms:` block. Applied to the running instance by swapping the bind-mounted file and restarting the one container — **no redeploy, no re-init**, so the master key and root token were never touched. Backup left at `/opt/app-src/databunker.yaml.bak`. The local file and the VM's are byte-identical, and the container confirms neither block is present inside it.

Nothing is dialled now: `sendCodeByPhoneDo` returns at `sms.go:18-21` on the missing gateway URL, and the SMTP path fails instantly on an empty server rather than reaching out to upstream's placeholder `email-smtp-server.com`.

## Re-verified after the edit

I re-ran the security check, because the file I edited is the one enforcing it:

- `/v1/status` → 200 `OK`
- root token still authenticates — **master key survived the restart**
- authenticated create works
- anonymous create still **403 Access denied**

## The one thing worth flagging

`default_country` lived inside the `sms:` block but has nothing to do with sending — it normalizes phone numbers on record creation. Deleting the block could plausibly have broken phone indexing, so I checked rather than assumed: `NormalizePhone` hard-codes a `GB` fallback on an empty value (`utils/utils.go:271-274`), which is exactly what upstream configured. Then I proved it on the live instance — a record created with `07700900123` was retrievable at `GET /v1/user/phone/+447700900123`, so the E.164 index is still being built correctly.

If you ever want a non-GB default, add `default_country` back **alone**, without a gateway URL.

## What this costs you

Only the data subject's own self-service login. The entire root-token API — create, read, update, delete, tokenization, consents, agreements, audit, backup — never sends anything and is unaffected. Record access is admin-mediated through your app, which is the shape this deployment is now committed to.

One trap to remember: `/v1/prelogin/...` returns `200 {"status":"ok","result":"done"}` whether or not delivery happened, because the send is a goroutine. That 200 is never evidence of delivery.

I recorded all of this in `redu.md` (now 32 quirks) — including an explicit "neither block may come back" note, since a future redeploy that copies the upstream file forward would silently reintroduce both. The `databunker.yaml` in this directory is the only correct source.

content.text:
Verified against the live instance — here's exactly how.

## Logging in

Open **https://databunker-t8agpc9v.redu.cloud/**

1. The dropdown defaults to **Email** — change it to **Root Token**.
2. Paste `de09418d-de93-4548-8de2-5cbcf281a234` into the token field.
3. Submit. **No captcha needed** — that's only enforced for the Email/Phone options.

You land on `/site/admin-view-requests.html`, with the audit log, data-subject requests and processing settings in the nav.

Under the hood it calls `GET /v1/userapps` with your token as `X-Bunker-Token`. I ran that call just now: **200** with your token, **403** without one. So the login path works and is properly gated.

## Two things to know before you use it

**The token goes into your browser's localStorage in plain text** (`localStorage['xtoken']`), and it stays there until cleared. That's the key to every personal record in the vault, with no reset if it leaks. Use it from a machine you trust, and clear site data on a shared one. There's no logout-invalidates-token concept here — the token is permanent.

**The Email and Phone options on that page are dead**, as expected — they're the data-subject self-service routes, and you removed both delivery channels. "Record Token" still works: a data subject with their record UUID can view their own data without any delivery channel, since it needs no code.

## One thing you may want to change

The login page pulls Bootstrap CSS from `stackpath.bootstrapcdn.com`. It's cosmetic, but it means your admin browser announces itself to a third-party CDN on every visit to a GDPR data vault — mildly at odds with the point of the thing. It's baked into the binary via packr, so changing it isn't a config edit; it'd need a custom image. Not worth doing unless it bothers you, but you should know it's there.

For API use rather than the UI, no login exists at all — just send the header:

```bash
curl -H "X-Bunker-Token: «REDACTED:assigned:5ee4b8b0»" \
  https://databunker-t8agpc9v.redu.cloud/v1/sys/configuration
```

content.text:
Yes for one, honestly qualified for the other two. Here's the precise state of each.

## 1. Root token — definitive, already working

Nothing to set up. It was created once by `-init` and I verified the exact call the UI makes (`GET /v1/userapps` → 200 with the token, 403 without). Select **Root Token** on the login page, paste the UUID. Done. This is the only one I've proven end-to-end on your instance.

## 2. Email — I know the config with certainty; I can't promise it works

The keys are exactly these, and the code reads no others:

```yaml
smtp:
  server: "smtp.yourprovider.com"
  port: 587
  user: "you@yourdomain.com"
  pass: "[REDACTED:value]"
  sender: "bot@yourdomain.com"
```

But four specific things in `email.go` mean I won't call this "definitely works" without testing it:

**Port 465 cannot work.** `smtp.SendMail` dials plaintext then upgrades via STARTTLS. Implicit-TLS on 465 needs a TLS dial first, which this code never does. You must use **587** (or 25).

**Your server must advertise STARTTLS.** Go's `smtp.PlainAuth` refuses to hand credentials to a non-TLS connection unless the host is localhost. A provider without STARTTLS on 587 fails outright.

**The message is malformed** — this is an upstream bug, not a config issue:

```go
msg := "From: "+sender+"\n" + "To: "+target+"\n" + "Subject: "+subject+"\n" + bodyMessage
```

There's **no blank line between the headers and the body**, and line endings are `\n` not `\r\n`. RFC 5322 ends headers at the first empty line, so `Access code is 123456` gets parsed as a broken header field. Strict MTAs reject it; lenient ones deliver an email with an empty body — meaning the user gets mail with no code in it.

**Envelope sender ≠ From header.** It passes `cfg.SMTP.User` as the envelope from while the `From:` header is `cfg.SMTP.Sender`. If those differ, SPF/DMARC or the relay may bounce it.

So: I know precisely *where* to put the settings. Getting mail actually delivered would likely need a patched image, not just config.

## 3. SMS — config shape is certain, and I'd advise against this build

```yaml
sms:
  url: "https://gateway.com/send?token=«REDACTED:assigned:3e755bf1»"
  # POST/JSON variant:
  # method: "POST"
  # content_type: "json"
  # body: '{"from":"_FROM_","to":"_PHONE_","message":"_MSG_"}'
  # basic_auth: "user:pass"
  # custom_header: "x-token: [REDACTED:value]"
```

**The placeholder trap:** upstream's own config comment documents the modifiers as `{token}, {from}, {phone}, {msg}` — but `sms.go:23-27` replaces `_TOKEN_`, `_FROM_`, `_PHONE_`, `_MSG_`. Follow the comment and your gateway receives a URL with a literal `{phone}` in it. The comment is simply wrong about its own code.

**The reason I'd leave this off:** `sms.go:43` and `:83` are both

```go
resp, _ := client.Do(req)
log.Println(resp.Status)
```

The error is discarded, and `client.Do` returns a **nil** response whenever it errors. So a DNS failure, refused connection, TLS error or timeout to your SMS gateway dereferences nil and panics — inside a bare `go sendCodeByPhone(...)` goroutine, with **no `recover()` anywhere in the codebase**. An unrecovered panic in a goroutine kills the whole process. Your vault goes down because an SMS provider had a bad minute. `restart: unless-stopped` brings it back, but it's repeatable.

## One constraint that hits both email and SMS

The login code expires **60 seconds** after it's generated (`users_db.go:100`), and it's single-use against that window. That's tight for SMS and frequently unrealistic for email — a code that lands in 90 seconds is already dead. Combined with the malformed-body bug, email self-service login on this build is marginal even when configured correctly.

---

None of this changes anything you've deployed — you've turned both off, and the crash vector above is a decent independent argument for that. If you ever do want the email path, the honest route is a patched image (fix the header separator, the `\r\n`, and the nil deref) rather than config alone. I can build that if it ever comes up.

content.text:
Yes — and I've already executed it once (in reverse), so it's tested, not theoretical.

## The two paths that matter

| | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **Source of truth** | `~/Desktop/tests_lib/databunker/databunker.yaml` | what a future redeploy ships |
| **Live** | `/opt/app-src/databunker.yaml` on the VM | bind-mounted to `/databunker/conf/databunker.yaml` |

Keep both in sync, or the next redeploy silently reverts the VM.

## Procedure — about a minute, no redeploy

```bash
cd ~/Desktop/tests_lib/databunker
# 1. edit databunker.yaml locally, adding the smtp: or sms: block

# 2. push it to the VM
cat databunker.yaml | ssh -i ~/.ssh/redu-deploy-test -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -p 22025 \
  ubuntu@databunker-t8agpc9v.redu.cloud 'sudo tee /opt/app-src/databunker.yaml > /dev/null'

# 3. restart just the long-running service
ssh -i ~/.ssh/redu-deploy-test -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -p 22025 \
  ubuntu@databunker-t8agpc9v.redu.cloud \
  'cd /opt/app-src && sudo docker compose restart databunker'
```

The init container is **not** re-run, so the master key and root token are untouched. That's what makes this the one safe change class here. Always re-run the anonymous-create check afterwards, since this file is what enforces that block.

## Where the credentials should go — and this differs per provider

I checked the config structs, and the two are not symmetric:

**SMTP has env-var support.** All five fields carry envconfig tags: `SMTP_SERVER`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`, `SMTP_SENDER`. So keep the password out of the YAML — pass it as an environment value and add it to the compose service's `environment:` block (that's a `docker compose up -d`, not just a restart).

One ordering trap: `ReadEnv` runs *before* `ReadConfFile`, and YAML only overwrites keys actually present in the document. So **omit `pass:` entirely** from the block. If you write `pass: ""`, that empty string clobbers your `SMTP_PASS`.

**SMS has no env-var support at all.** Every field — `url`, `token`, `basic_auth`, `custom_header` — is `yaml:` only, no envconfig tag. The gateway credential *must* live in the config file.

That matters because of the permissions I just checked on the VM:

```
-rw------- root:root    .env              ← 600, secrets safe
-rw-rw-r-- ubuntu:ubuntu databunker.yaml  ← 664, readable by any VM user
```

And it can't simply be tightened: the container runs as **`appuser` uid=100**, non-root, so `chmod 600 root:root` on that file would stop Databunker reading its own config at startup.

So an SMS gateway token on this deployment is necessarily world-readable to anyone with a shell on the VM. An SMTP password doesn't have to be. That asymmetry is a decent tiebreaker if you ever reconsider — SMTP is the one that can be done cleanly.

---

Unrelated but worth naming: the `woam` notice in that output flagging an "unexplained" container change at 20:51 is my own `docker compose restart` from the SMTP removal, not something else touching the box.
